To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a multi task learning framework using a Gaussian Process Tensor Regression (GPTR) model can be used to estimate normative brain models from neuroimaging data that can be used to detect individual variation from clinical populations and that the GPTR model outperforms both a mass univarite normative model and an SVM classifier that has access to clinical labels.

we propose a general, flexible, computationally affordable multi task learning framework for normative modeling of neuroimaging data that is based on tensor variate Gaussian processes and Kronecker algebra.

we propose a scalable multi-task Bayesian normative model that can be used to identify individual variation in brain structure and function and that this model substantially improves detection sensitivity in a clinical fMRI dataset.

developing scalable statistical models for normative modeling of neuroimaging data that are able to model structured variation across different dimensions and that can be applied to large datasets.

developing normative models of variation in neuroimaging data to support anomaly detection and clinical diagnosis.

the use of a multi-task learning framework with structured priors on the covariance can improve detection sensitivity of clinical anomalies in fMRI data.
a scalable multi task learning approach to neuroimaging analysis can be used to model complex patterns of correlation in neuroimaging data and that this can lead to improved detection performance.
